response.text:
Let \(q=1-p\), with  
\[
\mathbb P(\xi_i=1)=p,\qquad \mathbb P(\xi_i=-1)=q,
\]
where \(1/2<p<1\). Let \(\mathcal F_n=\sigma(\xi_1,\dots,\xi_n)\).

## (i) Martingale proof

For fixed \(\theta\ge 0\), define
\[
M_n(\theta)=\frac{e^{\theta S_n}}{\phi(\theta)^n},
\qquad 
\phi(\theta)=\mathbb E e^{\theta \xi_1}=pe^\theta+qe^{-\theta}.
\]
Then \((M_n(\theta))_{n\ge 0}\) is a martingale, because
\[
\mathbb E[M_{n+1}(\theta)\mid \mathcal F_n]
=
\frac{e^{\theta S_n}}{\phi(\theta)^{n+1}}
\mathbb E e^{\theta \xi_{n+1}}
=
\frac{e^{\theta S_n}}{\phi(\theta)^n}
=
M_n(\theta).
\]

Since \(p>q\), by the Strong Law of Large Numbers,
\[
\frac{S_n}{n}\to p-q>0 \quad \text{a.s.},
\]
so \(S_n\to +\infty\) a.s. Hence \(T_1<\infty\) a.s.

Now apply the Optional Stopping Theorem to the bounded stopping time \(T_1\wedge n\). We get
\[
1=\mathbb E M_{T_1\wedge n}(\theta).
\]
On \(\{T_1\le n\}\), we have \(S_{T_1}=1\), so
\[
M_{T_1}(\theta)=\frac{e^\theta}{\phi(\theta)^{T_1}}.
\]
Thus
\[
1
=
e^\theta \mathbb E\left[\phi(\theta)^{-T_1}\mathbf 1_{\{T_1\le n\}}\right]
+
\mathbb E\left[
\frac{e^{\theta S_n}}{\phi(\theta)^n}
\mathbf 1_{\{T_1>n\}}
\right].
\]
If \(T_1>n\), then the walk has not yet hit \(1\), so necessarily \(S_n\le 0\). Therefore, for \(\theta>0\),
\[
0\le 
\mathbb E\left[
\frac{e^{\theta S_n}}{\phi(\theta)^n}
\mathbf 1_{\{T_1>n\}}
\right]
\le \phi(\theta)^{-n}.
\]
Since \(\phi(\theta)>1\) for \(\theta>0\), this term tends to \(0\). For \(\theta=0\), the remainder term is simply \(\mathbb P(T_1>n)\to 0\).

Letting \(n\to\infty\), we obtain
\[
1=e^\theta \mathbb E\left[\phi(\theta)^{-T_1}\right].
\]
Hence
\[
\boxed{
e^\theta \mathbb E\left[\phi(\theta)^{-T_1}\right]=1
}
\qquad \text{for all } \theta\ge 0.
\]

---

## (ii) Computation of \(\mathbb E s^{T_1}\)

For \(\theta\ge 0\), \(\phi(\theta)\) is continuous and strictly increasing, because
\[
\phi'(\theta)=pe^\theta-qe^{-\theta}\ge p-q>0.
\]
Also \(\phi(0)=1\) and \(\phi(\theta)\to \infty\) as \(\theta\to\infty\). Therefore, for every \(s\in(0,1)\), there is a unique \(\theta>0\) such that
\[
\phi(\theta)=\frac1s.
\]
Using part (i),
\[
\mathbb E s^{T_1}
=
\mathbb E \phi(\theta)^{-T_1}
=
e^{-\theta}.
\]

Let \(x=e^\theta\). Then \(x>1\), and the equation \(\phi(\theta)=1/s\) becomes
\[
px+q x^{-1}=\frac1s.
\]
Multiplying by \(x\),
\[
p x^2-\frac1s x+q=0.
\]
Solving the quadratic,
\[
x
=
\frac{1\pm \sqrt{1-4pq s^2}}{2ps}.
\]
Since \(x=e^\theta>1\), we take the larger root:
\[
x=
\frac{1+\sqrt{1-4pq s^2}}{2ps}.
\]
Therefore
\[
\mathbb E s^{T_1}=e^{-\theta}=\frac1x
=
\frac{2ps}{1+\sqrt{1-4pq s^2}}.
\]
Equivalently, rationalizing,
\[
\boxed{
\mathbb E s^{T_1}
=
\frac{1-\sqrt{1-4pq s^2}}{2qs}
}
\qquad \text{for } 0<s<1.
\]
